# Task contract (generated by s01_problem from spec/protocol.yaml)

## Tasks and prediction time (1.1)
- Prediction time: `order_purchase_timestamp` (checkout).
- Regression: `lead_days` (days): order_delivered_customer_date - order_purchase_timestamp, fractional days; delivered orders with a valid lead time > 0.
- Classification: `is_detractor` (positive class 1): minimum valid review score <= 2 for an eligible order (not cancelled or unavailable, and reviewed). The score means the risk of a 1-2 star review if the customer reviews (scope limit).

## Stakeholders and action (1.2)
- Regression: logistics / fulfilment planning: expected lead time per order at checkout, to flag long-haul orders and set realistic delivery promises.
- Classification: customer-experience team: daily list of at-risk orders for proactive contact (status update, check with the seller).

## Targets and populations (1.3)
- Both tasks: orders purchased before data_start excluded (G-72); zero-item orders excluded; orders with missing payment_installments_max removed; orders without a usable payment removed (no payment rows, or only not_defined); orders with a negative value in a log1p candidate removed (zero kept).
- Regression: delivered orders with a valid lead time. Classification: orders not cancelled or unavailable, with a valid review; targets never imputed.
- Label sensitivity: is_detractor_first (first review only).

## Metrics (1.4)
- Regression: primary MAE; also rmse, r2, within_3d.
- Classification: primary AP; also roc_auc, brier, precision, recall, f1, confusion_matrix; accuracy is never reported alone.
- Charts: precision-recall and ROC curves out-of-fold (s06 6.6) and on test (s09), with curve data.
- Sources: Willmott, C. J. & Matsuura, K. (2005). Advantages of the mean absolute error (MAE) over the root mean square error (RMSE) in assessing average model performance. Climate Research 30:79-82.; Saito, T. & Rehmsmeier, M. (2015). The precision-recall plot is more informative than the ROC plot when evaluating binary classifiers on imbalanced datasets. PLoS ONE 10(3):e0118432.; Brier, G. W. (1950). Verification of forecasts expressed in terms of probability. Monthly Weather Review 78:1-3.

## Cost assumption (1.5)
- FN:FP = 5:1, an illustrative assumption, never measured ROI. Source: Elkan, C. (2001). The foundations of cost-sensitive learning. IJCAI 2001.

## Model families (1.6)
- Regression: dummy_median, linear, ridge, tree_reg, forest_reg. Classification: dummy_prior, logistic, tree_clf, forest_clf. Not used: boosting, voting, stacking.

## Decision rule (1.7)
- one-standard-error rule: keep the simplest candidate whose fold-mean primary metric is within one standard error of the best mean; SE = fold SD / sqrt(5); ties go to the simpler.
- Simplicity order: dummy < linear/logistic < single tree < forest; within a family: higher alpha, lower C, shallower depth, then larger leaf.
- the plain s06 model is kept if it is within one SE of the tuned configuration (G-55). Fallback: if no complex variant passes, the best simple model goes forward; if nothing beats the dummy, the dummy is the result. the rule recommends; the team confirms; an override is a logged protocol deviation (G-39, G-44).
- Alert threshold: minimise the illustrative cost subject to the daily alert cap, chosen by the team at the s08 hard stop.
- Sources: Breiman, L., Friedman, J., Olshen, R. & Stone, C. (1984). Classification and Regression Trees.; Hastie, T., Tibshirani, R. & Friedman, J. (2009). The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., section 7.10.; Friedman, J., Hastie, T. & Tibshirani, R. (2010). Regularization paths for generalized linear models via coordinate descent. Journal of Statistical Software 33(1).

## Search budget (1.8)
- Grids fixed in advance (see protocol.yaml `grids`); forest 200 trees; seed 42. Source: Breiman, L. (2001). Random forests. Machine Learning 45:5-32.

## Scope limits
- Checkout-time information only; populations are fulfilled (regression) and reviewed (classification) orders.
- The cost ratio is illustrative; no causal claims.
